policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the main text passively, 'our horn shall be exalted,' matching the qere/base; its mapped textual-variant note assigns 'thou shalt exalt our horn' to the other reading.
ASV 'will I keep' does not distinguish the qere from the ketiv, and the mapped note 'Or, be faithful' is classed alternative_rendering, so it cannot decide the textual reading.
